touches.text: Nodes: one long list, id = row. Every tree indexes it; no tree owns a node, so several trees can index the same node in different ways.

Embeddings. Not every node gets one. WHY: embedding every single thing would make an impossible mound of data, and that is not how Akien works, and this is meant to work the way he does. What gets embedded is the pattern: the answers to a few key questions that cross domains (4.3.1.8). A node without an embedding is found by its key (eg an exact request).

The walk. The string is cut into words deterministically (stems, no LLM). Start at the top; at each node score each child by how much of the string's words it has seen before, weighted by the counts; step to the best child; stop at a leaf, or when no child scores above the floor (a setting, measured). The result is the path taken, with each step's score.

The bench. The trees are learned by watching them run, so the first thing built on them is a way to see them: a graph-trees pane on the librarian's page (15) that draws a tree, takes a string and a question, lights the path with its scores, shows the embedding and the miss when there is one, and walks two strings from two domains side by side to see whether they land together; and the same from the command line, `cairn librarian walk "<string>" for <question>` (8.4.5). Every number in 4.3.1.9 (the floor, the buckets, the merge rule) is a setting, so an experiment is changing one and walking again. WHY: "i can imagine being able to understand it once i can run experiments and see what happens." Nothing in 4.3.1.9 is known until this has measured it (Law 3).

walk, nearest, neighbors: not the verbs a device uses; the librarian encapsulates them under ask (4.5.3). `walk "<string>" for <question>` is also the bench's verb for the operator (4.3.1.10): diagnostic, showing the path and scores, never how a device asks.
The trees tool's charter lists in its public interface what it offers: the module, and deposit_keyed, find and the keyed leaf's shape beside it. Akien 2026-11-09, answering Q#77.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model: a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation, asking "what did this request answer?". An answer is found by its exact request and carries no embedding (4.3.1.6). The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27). The inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock, is only for debugging.
